abstract: Congenital obstructive uropathy (COU) is an important cause of childhood kidney failure, yet understanding its variable renal outcomes and genetic modifiers is limited by the lack of genotype-independent models of in utero obstruction. Here, we characterized renal morphology and gene expression at embryonic day (E)18.5 in a mouse model of COU induced by exposure to 2,3,7,8-tetrachlorodibenzo-p-dioxin (dioxin) at E10.5. Dioxin exposure reproducibly induced bilateral hydroureteronephrosis with selective medullary flattening with relatively preserved renal architecture. Transcriptomic analysis revealed altered developmental, cell cycle, metabolic, innate immune, and toxin response programs, alongside changes in cell-type-associated signatures. However, immunohistochemistry showed no differences in the abundance of examined stromal and proximal tubular populations, suggesting altered cellular states rather than changes in cellular composition. Together with morphology consistent with early obstructive responses and the absence of prominent injury markers, these findings support its use as a non-genetic model to investigate how congenital obstruction perturbs renal development.
